target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type) (T : ℕ) (Q : S1 X Y → Prop),
    (∀ N, N.D9 → Q N) → (∃ N, Q N) →
    ∀ c4 : ({xs : List X // xs.length ≤ T} → Y) → Prop,
      ∃ N : S1 X Y, ¬ (Q N ↔ c4 (N.d24 T))
a_raw: {"translation": "`Target` defines a proposition (it names a `Prop` without asserting or proving it). In this proposition, for types `X` and `Y`, a system `N : S1 X Y` consists of: a finite type of nodes `A1`; an arbitrary state type `A3 n` for each node `n : A1`; an initial global state `a4` assigning an element of `A3 n` to each `n : A1`; a local update function `a5` taking a node `n`, a global state `σ : (m : A1) → A3 m`, and an input `x : X` to a next state in `A3 n`; and a readout function `a6` mapping a global state to `Y`. A system `N` satisfies `N.D9` if its dependency graph has no directed cycles of length at least 1 (including self-loops): specifically, for no node `n : N.A1` is there a finite nonempty chain `n = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n` (`k ≥ 1`) where each step `N.D8 c_i c_{i+1}` holds, meaning `c_{i+1}`'s update depends on `c_i`'s state (there exist global states `σ, σ'` agreeing on every node `k ≠ c_i` and an input `x : X` such that `N.a5 c_{i+1} σ x ≠ N.a5 c_{i+1} σ' x`). For a natural number `T`, `N.d24 T` is the function mapping each finite input sequence `xs : List X` of length at most `T` to `N.a6` applied to the global state obtained by starting at `N.a4` and synchronously updating all nodes via `fun σ x n => N.a5 n σ x` for each element of `xs` from left to right. In full, `Target` is the proposition: for all types `X` and `Y`, for every natural number `T`, and for every predicate `Q` on `S1 X Y`, if (1) every system `N : S1 X Y` satisfying `N.D9` satisfies `Q N`, and (2) there exists at least one system `N : S1 X Y` satisfying `Q N`, then for every predicate `c4` on functions from `X`-sequences of length at most `T` to `Y`, there exists a system `N : S1 X Y` (which may depend on `X`, `Y`, `T`, `Q`, and `c4`) such that `Q N` and `c4 (N.d24 T)` do not have the same truth value (i.e., `¬ (Q N ↔ c4 (N.d24 T))`, meaning one holds and the other fails). Regarding what is and is not required: `X` and `Y` are completely arbitrary types (with no nonemptiness, finiteness, or cardinality assumptions); `T` is any natural number (including `0`); `c4` is an arbitrary predicate with no restrictions; and the witness `N` in the conclusion is not required to satisfy `N.D9` or any bound on its number of nodes. Notably, as written, hypothesis (2) only requires that `Q` hold for at least one system (`∃ N, Q N`) and there is no hypothesis requiring `Q` to fail for any system, so `Q` is permitted to hold for every `N : S1 X Y`."}
translation: `Target` defines a proposition (it names a `Prop` without asserting or proving it). In this proposition, for types `X` and `Y`, a system `N : S1 X Y` consists of: a finite type of nodes `A1`; an arbitrary state type `A3 n` for each node `n : A1`; an initial global state `a4` assigning an element of `A3 n` to each `n : A1`; a local update function `a5` taking a node `n`, a global state `σ : (m : A1) → A3 m`, and an input `x : X` to a next state in `A3 n`; and a readout function `a6` mapping a global state to `Y`. A system `N` satisfies `N.D9` if its dependency graph has no directed cycles of length at least 1 (including self-loops): specifically, for no node `n : N.A1` is there a finite nonempty chain `n = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n` (`k ≥ 1`) where each step `N.D8 c_i c_{i+1}` holds, meaning `c_{i+1}`'s update depends on `c_i`'s state (there exist global states `σ, σ'` agreeing on every node `k ≠ c_i` and an input `x : X` such that `N.a5 c_{i+1} σ x ≠ N.a5 c_{i+1} σ' x`). For a natural number `T`, `N.d24 T` is the function mapping each finite input sequence `xs : List X` of length at most `T` to `N.a6` applied to the global state obtained by starting at `N.a4` and synchronously updating all nodes via `fun σ x n => N.a5 n σ x` for each element of `xs` from left to right. In full, `Target` is the proposition: for all types `X` and `Y`, for every natural number `T`, and for every predicate `Q` on `S1 X Y`, if (1) every system `N : S1 X Y` satisfying `N.D9` satisfies `Q N`, and (2) there exists at least one system `N : S1 X Y` satisfying `Q N`, then for every predicate `c4` on functions from `X`-sequences of length at most `T` to `Y`, there exists a system `N : S1 X Y` (which may depend on `X`, `Y`, `T`, `Q`, and `c4`) such that `Q N` and `c4 (N.d24 T)` do not have the same truth value (i.e., `¬ (Q N ↔ c4 (N.d24 T))`, meaning one holds and the other fails). Regarding what is and is not required: `X` and `Y` are completely arbitrary types (with no nonemptiness, finiteness, or cardinality assumptions); `T` is any natural number (including `0`); `c4` is an arbitrary predicate with no restrictions; and the witness `N` in the conclusion is not required to satisfy `N.D9` or any bound on its number of nodes. Notably, as written, hypothesis (2) only requires that `Q` hold for at least one system (`∃ N, Q N`) and there is no hypothesis requiring `Q` to fail for any system, so `Q` is permitted to hold for every `N : S1 X Y`.

divergences.description: Missing negation in the feedforward premise: `Target` assumes `(∀ N, N.D9 → Q N)`, which says every acyclic (feedforward) system satisfies `Q` (is conscious), reversing the source passage ([P-D51a]: feedforward systems are never conscious) and the author's claim ('calls no feedforward system conscious'), which require `(∀ N, N.D9 → ¬ Q N)`. Because the other premise `(∃ N, Q N)` has the same polarity on `Q` (even if one tried to read `Q` as 'unconscious', it would require `∃ N, ¬ Q N`), `Target` is actually false as written (e.g., take `X = Y = Unit`, `T = 0`, `Q := fun _ => True`, and `c4 := fun _ => True`).

Physical systems and input-output functions from [P-D53] are idealized as deterministic, synchronous, discrete-time finite-node networks (`S1 X Y`) with a fixed initial state whose input-output behaviour is compared only up to a finite horizon `T` (`N.d24 T`), and P1/P3/P4 are collapsed into requiring the empirical inference `c4` to be a total `Prop`-valued function of that `T`-step input-output map.

A causal structure theory from [P-D51a] is weakened/abstracted to an arbitrary binary predicate `Q : S1 X Y → Prop` (without requiring `Q` to depend on causal structure, invoke `ϕ`, or classify all recurrent systems as conscious). Once the missing negation is restored, this weakens the hypothesis and thus harmlessly strengthens the theorem.

Compared to Kleiner and Hoel's framework in [P-K33] (and `S3` in the context), `Target` specializes falsification to a deterministic binary truth-value mismatch `¬ (Q N ↔ c4 (N.d24 T))` rather than set-valued predictions over an experience space or an `or`-falsification tied to a specific fixed inference content `or`.

judgement.summary: The formalization is divergent because it omits a negation in `(∀ N, N.D9 → Q N)`, assuming every feedforward system is conscious instead of none; this reverses the causal-structure-theory premise and renders `Target` false as stated.
